faq: Can I text my existing customer list?

Only people who gave clear written permission to receive marketing texts. Buying a number list, or texting customers who only gave a number at checkout without consent, is not allowed, and we will not do it.
Which countries and carriers are covered?
Our set-up is built for the United States and Canada rules, and we can advise on other regions. Some countries need extra registration, which takes time that is outside our control.
Which SMS tools do you use?
Klaviyo, Postscript, Attentive, Omnisend and Shopify's own text tools are common. You pay the tool and the carrier fees directly, and our price covers only the work.
How many texts should I send?
Far fewer than emails. We usually start with two to four a month, each with a clear reason, and watch the stop rate. If unsubscribes rise, we reduce the number.

desc:
SMS marketing campaigns for opted-in customers reach people where they read first: their phone. Ecom Swift LLC sets up text campaigns in your own tool, writes short messages, checks consent wording and schedules sends at sensible times.

## What are SMS marketing campaigns?

SMS marketing campaigns are text messages a business sends to customers who agreed to receive them. Each message is short, names the business, carries one link or action and offers a clear way to stop. They suit time-sensitive news such as a sale starting, a restock or a delivery update.

Because texts arrive on a personal device, they feel closer than email. That closeness is useful when the message is welcome and harmful when it is not, which is why consent comes first.

## Why careful texting matters

A text is read quickly, so you have only a line or two to say something useful. A vague or too-frequent message can lead people to reply STOP, and a lost opt-in is hard to win back. Careful texting protects the list you worked to build.

Consent also matters beyond courtesy. Rules about who may be texted, what must be disclosed and when messages may be sent differ by country and region, and carriers can block senders who ignore them. We build campaigns around clear opt-in wording, your business name in every message, an easy opt-out and quiet hours by time zone. We do not give legal advice, so for specific legal questions you should consult a qualified adviser.

## What a good SMS program includes

- Opt-in wording on each signup form that states what the person will receive and how to stop.
- Messages that start with your business name, so the sender is obvious.
- One purpose per text: a launch, a restock, a reminder or a thank-you.
- A short, tracked link so you can see which texts get clicks.
- A STOP reply handled by your tool, with unsubscribes respected at once.
- Quiet hours set by the recipient's time zone.
- A welcome text for new subscribers, confirming what they signed up for.
- Segments, such as recent buyers, so offers fit the reader.
- Picture messages used sparingly, where an image helps.
- A simple guide to reading replies and campaign results.

## How we set it up

We work in your own SMS or email and SMS tool. First we review the opt-in wording on your forms and check how phone numbers are collected and stored. Then we write the campaigns in plain, short language, set the send times and add link tracking.

The Basic package covers two scheduled campaigns and a review of one form. Standard adds more campaigns, a welcome text, a segment and a short reply-handling guide. Premium adds automated texts such as cart and back-in-stock messages, picture messages, segments for buyers and browsers, and a results review with a handover call. We only schedule sends to people with a recorded opt-in.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Text only people who clearly agreed.
- Say who you are in the first words.
- Keep each message to one idea and one link.
- Send in daytime hours for the reader's time zone.
- Reply to customer questions quickly, because texts invite conversation.

**Avoid:**
- Importing an old email list and texting it without consent.
- Sending the same text to everyone, every week.
- Using all capitals and heavy urgency.
- Hiding the opt-out.
- Sending a text when an email would do the same job.

## Who it is for

This service suits a store with a growing list and a recent habit of collecting phone numbers at checkout. It fits a local brand that has timely news, such as limited drops or pickup reminders. It also suits a business that tried texting once, saw complaints and wants a more careful restart.

## What we need from you

Tell us which SMS tool you use, or ask us to suggest what fits your store. Send your brand name, tone preferences, the dates you want to promote and the form where phone numbers are collected. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the tool supports it, and you remain the account owner.
